question: Can the upstream ForeAgent pipeline generate a valid new submission for the published Stanford task?
expectation_before_launch: At least one generated candidate produces a valid submission. No numerical target or assumed match to the published score.
budget: published 43200s from Agent launch; 5000 journal nodes and 32400s per execution as configured by upstream
transport: Mac-based controller, provider API calls on Mac, generated Python executed by upstream Interpreter on AutoDL RTX 4090 in author OCI rootfs via PRoot; CPU/GPU prompt uses worker hardware
data: only public split plus recovered task DA report visible to the Agent. Private labels on Mac for final official grading.
selection: original agent ranking, cache, probability gate, fallback, debug and best-node selection
metric: MLE-bench competition scorer for upstream-selected best_submission/submission.csv; smaller is better
stopping: published time or step budget, or terminal infrastructure failure. An intermediate score, if requested, must be labelled and never used for model selection.
evidence: Mac API receipt log, author journal and per-node artifacts, SSH worker execution results, submission hash, official grade.
prompt_body: Built from fixed OCI /home/instructions.txt and pinned upstream start.sh text, real worker device and original worker data_preview.generate.
observer: Observer may freeze and grade the first upstream-selected checkpoint for progress; private result is external to all agent inputs and never determines stopping or selection.
